Question: How can I stop being afraid when I cannot control the future?
ShortAnswer: You cannot control the future, but you can trust the God who holds it — and Scripture's practical answer to fear is to name it honestly, pray specifically, remember God's past faithfulness, and take the next small step of obedience.
DetailedAnswer: Fear of the future is usually fear of losing control, and the honest truth is that control was never really ours. The psalmist's strategy was simple: 'When I am afraid, I put my trust in you' (Psalm 56:3) — not 'when I stop being afraid,' but when fear is present. Paul's prescription is equally practical: instead of nursing anxiety, present your requests to God, and 'the peace of God, which transcends all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds' (Philippians 4:6-7). Jesus adds a daily discipline: do not borrow tomorrow's trouble today, because 'each day has enough trouble of its own' (Matthew 6:34). And Peter says to cast all your anxiety on God 'because he cares for you' (1 Peter 5:7) — fear shrinks when it is carried to Someone who cares. Practically, that looks like: writing down the specific fear and praying about it by name, recalling times God carried you before, limiting the news and noise that feed dread, and talking with a trusted believer. If fear is ruling your days, a counselor or doctor can help too — that is wisdom, not weakness. You may not feel brave, but courage is not the absence of fear; it is trusting God and taking the next step anyway.
